source: Battle facts (CWSAC battle CSV + American Battlefield Trust) for the 60th NY's engagements
method: Downloaded the CWSAC battle CSV in full (393 rows) from GitHub raw; corroborated against American Battlefield Trust pages. NOTE: the CSV has NO standalone 'Lookout Mountain' row — Lookout Mountain (Nov 24 1863) is subsumed under the Chattanooga battle (TN024). Reported as actual CSV rows, not an invented row.

battles.name: Lookout Mountain (within Chattanooga)
battles.csv_verbatim_key_fields: TN024 | Chattanooga | TN | Hamilton County / City of Chattanooga | Chattanooga-Ringgold Campaign [Nov 1863] | 1863-11-23 → 1863-11-25 | Union victory | casualties 12,485 (US 5,815; CS 6,670) | significance A
battles.abt_verbatim: American Battlefield Trust: 'the Battle of Lookout Mountain occurred on November 24, 1863'; Hooker's attack on the Confederate left; 'By 2:00 pm, the "Battle Among the Clouds" was over.'
battles.relevance: Alexander (Sergeant, Co. H) was WOUNDED here Nov 24 1863, per Eddy's casualty list. The 60th NY 'captured one cannon and battle flag' (NYSMM). Cached: shared/battle-details/lookout-mountain.json.

battles.name: Wauhatchie / Brown's Ferry (Lookout Valley, the 'Cracker Line')
battles.csv_verbatim_key_fields: TN021 | Wauhatchie (Brown's Ferry) | TN | Hamilton/Marion/Dade Co. | Reopening the Tennessee River [Oct 1863] | 1863-10-28 → 1863-10-29 | Union victory | 828 total (US 420; CS 408) | significance B; forces 'XI Corps and 2nd Division, XII Corps [US]' (the 60th NY's corps)
battles.relevance: Context for the 60th NY's arrival in the Chattanooga theatre weeks before Lookout Mountain.

battles.name: Gettysburg (Culp's Hill)
battles.csv_verbatim_key_fields: PA002 | Gettysburg | PA | Adams County | Gettysburg Campaign [Jun-Jul 1863] | 1863-07-01 → 1863-07-03 | Union victory | strength 158,300 | casualties 51,000 (US 23,000; CS 28,000) | significance A; description references Culp's Hill ('the Confederate infantry were driven from their last toe-hold on Culp's Hill')
battles.relevance: The 60th NY held Culp's Hill (extreme left of the 12th Corps) — the family-tradition site where descendant Alexander Hubbell Levitt was later named (G03). At Gettysburg the 60th lost 11 killed + 39 wounded (NYSMM).

notes: Battle facts are unit/event-level (not person-level); they situate Alexander's documented wound (Lookout Mountain) and the family's Culp's Hill tradition.
